messages:
Maria: Heads-up — seeing a sudden spike in preemptions/evictions in ap-southeast1c the last 20m. Cost also jumped. Tiny GPU pods are getting bounced. Anyone oncall or seen this? :thinking:
SRE-bot: ALERT: eviction_rate[gpu-ap-southeast1c] = 6.7/min (threshold 2.0). Rolling 10m window.
Aj: Can you paste the pod list and node labels?
Maria: quick dump: ```kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running | grep tiny | wc -l
> 82
kubectl describe node gpu-node-112 | grep -E "Labels:|Taints:"
> Labels: gpu.family=rtxA, zone=ap-southeast1c, nodepool=prod-compact
> Taints: nvidia.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule
```
Kyle: We started rolling gpu.family label enforcement last week to force newer SKUs into prod. Looks like a bunch of tiny pods still request older-family affinity which causes tight packing -> fragmentation.
Samir: If they're tiny pods (1 GPU or fractional), the scheduler is struggling to co-locate them because of required nodeAffinity + taints. Two quick mitigations: 1) bump warm-pool for that AZ, 2) temporarily convert requiredDuringScheduling nodeAffinity to preferred.
Lena: I can lift warmpool from 6 -> 12 for ap-southeast1c as a short-term. That buys time while we audit workloads.
Aj: Before changing affinity, can we confirm scheduler logs? Maria can you grab a sample bind failure?
Maria: snippet from scheduler logs: ```I0323 09:12:45.123 scheduler_binder.go:214] Binding failed for pod ml/tiny-worker-289: no nodes available that match nodeAffinity (gpu.family in [rtx7 rtxa]) and tolerations: "nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule"```
Kyle: there we go. Many pods are still built against rtx7/rtxa. The label rollout made those nodes incompatible. The mix of strict affinity + taints + small pod sizes means we have many single-GPU pods stranded and evicting when larger jobs land.
Samir: Agreed. Short-term plan: Lena will increase warmpool; Maria will patch one critical microservice to relax nodeAffinity to preferred (canary 10%); Aj will open a ticket to audit pod specs and add an operator to flag strict gpu.family requests.
Lena: Increasing warm pool now. Running: ```./infractl warmpool scale --region ap-southeast1 --az c --pool prod-compact --count 12```
SRE-bot: RUNBOOK: warmpool scale triggered by Lena at 2025-03-23T09:19:33Z (run id rp-4521).
Maria: Patching canary microservice spec: switching required->preferred for nodeAffinity, pushing rollout to 10% via kustomize overlay. ```kubectl patch deployment tiny-svc -n ml -p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"affinity": {"nodeAffinity": {"requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution": null, "preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution": [{"weight": 100, "preference": {"matchExpressions": [{"key": "gpu.family", "operator": "In", "values": ["rtx7","rtxa"]}]}}]}}}}}}'```
Aj: Nice. Also we should temporarily relax the binpack threshold so small pods can co-locate with larger ones (set pack imbalance tolerance to 0.15). I'll make a quick config change on staging first.
Kyle: Long-term: we should either (A) migrate residual rtx7 workloads, (B) make nodeAffinity an opt-in for new builds, or (C) add a packing-aware scheduler plugin that understands fractional GPUs.
Maria: Opening ticket TICKET-4521: "ap-southeast1c tiny-pod eviction wave — affinity/taint fragmentation" and assigning to infra + runtime. Will include audit list and candidate mitigations.
Samir: After warmpool bump and canary, monitor eviction_rate and cost. If evictions don't drop in 30m, we fallback to temporarily lifting taints on rtxA nodes and cordoning the problematic nodepool for rolling update.
SRE-bot: METRIC: eviction_rate[gpu-ap-southeast1c] now 0.9/min (was 6.7). Noted decreased trend.
Maria: Good, keep watching. Thanks all — follow-ups in TICKET-4521. :thumbsup:
